content: Oh yes, some seriously good stuff. It’s time to crack the Croatian liqueurs.
only 2,670 **days** between these two photos We’ve come a long way

I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code written by coding agents - here's a description of the external sandbox pattern, where agents run on your Mac but execute code in a WebAssembly or QEMU or Apple Container sandbox - with demos for Claude Code, Codex and Pi https://blog.primeradiant.com/external-sandboxes-for-coding-agents/

I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers - here's our index repository for these external sandbox prototypes https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/external-sandbox

Each of the three sandbox servers includes an optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxy, so you can control exactly which hosts your agent's code can communicate with - plus a credential replacement mechanism to make authenticated API calls without sharing a secret with the agent

A lot of folks don't realize how much of our computer infrastructure is an improvised system prone to cascading failures. You didn't need offensive AI cyberattacks to have big outages like Microsoft/FAA. Of course, now we DO have to deal with offensive AI (but also defensive AIs)

I say this as I see every outage of the last five days get picked up by people who did not pay attention to cybersecurity before, usually with the implication that "this is the big one," which, in turn, leads people on both X and real life to panic and spread further rumors.

I will say that the Mythos security freakout, much derided at the time, and the focus on first deploying cyber models with limited access from the Labs seems to have been an effective step in mitigating some of the downside cyber risk that would have otherwise happened from AI.
